title: TypeScript: types
summary: Add types to variables, arrays and functions so mistakes are caught before the app runs.

quiz.q: Which line is valid TypeScript for a variable that must hold a whole or decimal number?
quiz.explain: The primitive type is the lowercase `number`. It covers whole and decimal values. The type goes after the name, separated by a colon.

quiz.q: Complete the type of an array of text values.
quiz.explain: `string[]` means an array where every item is a string. `Array<string>` means the same.

quiz.q: Click the line that TypeScript will report as an error.
quiz.explain: `age` was declared as a number, so assigning the text 'nineteen' is a type error. TypeScript tells you this in the editor, before the code runs.

quiz.q: What does `: number` after the parentheses mean in `function double(n: number): number`?
options: The function must be called twice
quiz.explain: The type after the parameter list is the return type. The type inside the parentheses (`n: number`) is the parameter type.

exercise.task:
Complete `types.ts` by adding types.

- Annotate `studentName` as a `string`.
- Annotate `marks` as a `number`.
- Annotate `passed` as a `boolean`.
- Annotate `subjects` as an array of strings.
- Type the function `average`: parameters `a` and `b` are numbers and it returns a number.
hints: A type annotation is written after the name: `name: type`.
For the array use `string[]`. For the function put types on both parameters and after the closing parenthesis.

checks.name: subjects is an array of strings
checks.hint: Use string[] (or Array<string>) after the name.

checks.name: average has number parameters and a number return type
checks.hint: Write: function average(a: number, b: number): number

checks.name: average returns the mean of a and b
